faqs.question: What is a safety canister for in-plant use?
faqs.answer: It's a stainless steel container built for the safe storage, filling, and metering of flammable liquids within a plant, with removable flame traps and a pressure control valve for protection.

faqs.question: Can this canister be used for off-site transport?
faqs.answer: No. This product is certified for in-plant use only; off-site transport requires a separately certified transportation container.

faqs.question: What is the difference between this canister and the Safety Can?
faqs.answer: The Canister is built for larger volumes (5 to 20 liters versus the Can's 1 to 5 liters), uses thicker 0.8 mm steel, supports horizontal storage, and offers four dispensing mechanisms instead of two.

faqs.question: Can this canister be stored horizontally?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the self-closing tap variants, which are specifically built for horizontal storage and filling.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the four dispensing mechanisms?
faqs.answer: Use the self-closing metering device for controlled dosing, the ventilated version at 20 liters for smoother high-volume pouring, the screw cap for simple access, or the ventilated tap for horizontal storage and dispensing.

faqs.question: How do I find the exact order number for my requirement?
faqs.answer: Confirm your size (5, 10, or 20 liters) and dispensing mechanism; for example, a 10-liter canister with a screw cap is order number 10KK.

faqs.question: Is the ventilated metering device available in every size?
faqs.answer: No. It's only available at 20 liters; the 5 and 10-liter metering devices don't include separate ventilation.

faqs.question: How much space does this canister actually save versus glass bottles?
faqs.answer: Rötzmeier states the canister shape saves cabinet, cupboard, and shelf space specifically compared to glass bottles; Inkarp can confirm the exact difference against your current storage.

faqs.question: Can the flame traps be serviced?
faqs.answer: Yes. They're removable, supporting inspection and maintenance rather than replacing the entire unit.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Safety Canisters for In-Plant Use in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the size and dispensing mechanism you need. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

longForm.heroLead: A glass bottle takes up the space it takes up, standing upright, every time. This canister doesn't have to. Its self-closing tap versions are built for horizontal storage and filling, and the canister shape itself saves real space in a safety cabinet, laboratory cupboard, or shelf, specifically compared to bottles. Stainless steel at 0.8 mm, thicker than a standard safety can, with a solid stainless steel handhold built for repeated handling. The flame traps are removable, so they can be inspected and serviced rather than replaced as a whole unit. Four dispensing mechanisms cover different needs: a self-closing metering device for controlled dosing, the same device with separate ventilation at 20 liters, a screw cap for simple access, or a self-closing tap with separate ventilation for horizontal use. This canister is built for in-plant use. Off-site transport requires a certified transportation container instead.

sections.title: Safety Canisters for In-Plant Use at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate these canisters: how horizontal storage actually saves space, which of the four dispensing mechanisms fits your workflow, what sizes and order numbers are available, and Inkarp installation and service support.
sections.subheading: Storage is named as its own function, not an afterthought to dispensing.
body: These canisters are built for safe storage, filling, and metering, not just active transfer.
Horizontal storage is a real capability, not a marketing angle. The self-closing tap variants are specifically built for horizontal storage and filling, which changes how they fit into a cabinet.
The space savings are stated against a specific comparison. Rötzmeier states the canister shape saves space in safety cabinets, cupboards, and shelves, particularly compared to glass bottles.
Construction is heavier than the Safety Can line. 0.8 mm stainless steel and a solid stainless steel handhold, built for larger volumes and repeated handling.
Flame traps can be serviced, not just replaced. They're removable, which supports inspection and maintenance over the canister's working life.

Four dispensing mechanisms serve four different needs. A metering device for controlled dosing, the same device with separate ventilation at 20 liters, a screw cap for simple access, or a ventilated tap for horizontal use.
This is an in-plant product, and that boundary matters. Off-site transport requires a certified transportation container, a genuinely separate Rötzmeier line.

Configuration note: Confirmed line is the Rötzmeier Safety Canisters - for in-plant use. Available sizes are 5, 10 and 20 liters. Four dispensing mechanisms: self-closing metering device, self-closing metering device with separate ventilation (20 L only), screw cap, self-closing tap with separate ventilation. Not certified for off-site transport - a separate product line covers that requirement. Full specifications (exact dimensions, weight, additional certification detail) are available on request from Inkarp.

body: The technical specifications of the Safety Canisters for In-Plant Use include 0.8 mm stainless steel construction, a 0.3 bar pressure valve, and four dispensing mechanisms.
Most flammable liquid storage assumes a container standing upright, which is exactly the assumption this canister's shape and tap design don't require.

The self-closing tap variants are purpose-built for horizontal storage and filling, which changes what actually fits in a safety cabinet or on a shelf. Rötzmeier states the canister form itself saves space compared to bottles, glass ones specifically, which matters directly in a cabinet where every centimeter of shelf space is already accounted for.
Product expert note: Tell our team your cabinet dimensions and current bottle sizes, and Inkarp will confirm the space savings for your specific setup.

sections.title: Dispensing Mechanisms, Ventilation and Order Numbers
body: Four dispensing mechanisms exist because four different jobs need different things from a canister.

For precise, repeated small-volume dosing, specify the self-closing metering device. For high-volume dosing with smoother pour control, specify the ventilated metering device at 20 liters. For straightforward fill-and-pour access, specify the screw cap. For horizontal storage in a space-limited cabinet, specify the self-closing tap with separate ventilation.
